applicability_rule: APPLICABLE only to Tested Code that contains an exact-equality comparison against an account/token balance (a construct of the form `<balance-expression> == <specified amount or variable>`, e.g. `address(this).balance == x` or `token.balanceOf(a) == b`). NOT_APPLICABLE to code with no such exact-equality balance check.

derivation_log_entry.basis_classification_rationale: Explicit in the requirement's own scope clause ('Tested code that checks whether the balance of an account is exactly equal to ... a specified amount or the value of a variable'), matching L1's is_unconditioned_subject=False.
derivation_log_entry.derivation_method: L1 conditioned_scope_clause field, confirmed by direct reading

cross_reference_note: This requirement is the M-level Overriding Requirement for req-1-exact-balance-check (S) -- and its applicability trigger is IDENTICAL to that S requirement's own trigger (same 'exact balance check' pattern). This is a structural pattern worth generalizing in Track B: S/M override pairs frequently share one applicability trigger, differing only in what conformance obligation applies once triggered (S: 'don't do this check at all'; M: 'if you do this check, also protect against transfers affecting it'). Not yet verified whether this pattern holds for all S/M override pairs in the full 81-requirement corpus -- flagged as a Track B hypothesis, not assumed to generalize.
